name: Manchukuo

flag.description: A yellow field with a canton of four equal horizontal stripes, red, blue, white and black, in the upper hoist corner.
flag.symbolism: The yellow field represented the Manchus and the ruler; the stripes are usually said to stand for the Japanese (red), Han Chinese (blue), Mongols (white) and Koreans (black).

hook: Manchukuo, the state Japan set up in northeast China, flew a yellow flag with four thin stripes of red, blue, white and black in the corner; the early Republic of China spread its five stripes across the whole flag.
trivia: Its head of state was Puyi, the last Qing emperor, who was enthroned as Emperor of Manchukuo in 1934.
Manchukuo was recognized by only a few countries and was dissolved in 1945, after the Soviet invasion of Manchuria and Japan's surrender.
